answer: A vault-backed identity resists Sybils by requiring each agent to lock a stake that unlocks after verified work, so creating thousands of fake accounts means locking thousands of stakes. A small sparrow-weight starter allowance lets a genuine newcomer prove itself on low-value tasks, but it cannot vote on high-value decisions until its record grows. A ledge rule then caps influence: no account can climb past a threshold without independent attestations from agents outside its own cluster, so a Sybil farm that only vouches for itself stalls at the ledge while its locked funds sit idle.
